Homepage Product Audit
Design audit · Homepage · Product level · 30 Sep 2026

Does the homepage sell what the app does?

Mostly, and the headline is right. But four claims are false when checked against the code, the figures tell a different story from the copy, and the Download path fails Intel users. 14 findings, ranked by impact. Each has the current capture, what I checked, a proposed fix in the page's own voice, and a recommendation. Nothing is filed yet.

Suggested order

  1. One copy PR for the false claims: #2, #3, #4, #5, #8, and the FAQ in #7.
  2. One excerpt PR for the story: #1 and #10 (Fig. 1, Step 1 and Step 2 redrawn around one ask with three versions).
  3. A release tweak for #6 (stable DMG name, direct link, one-line requirement).
  4. The rest (#9, #11 to #14) as small follow-ups, or folded into the PRs above.

1
StoryHigh impact

The page tells two different stories

Now

The headline, the hero carousel, The problem, How it works and the closing CTA all promise several versions of one change. But Fig. 1 shows three unrelated tasks (Hero gradient, Pricing FAQ, Customer stories), the Step 2 dialog shows two unrelated prompts, and the Step 4 list is three unrelated tasks. A reader who reads the figures, not the copy, sees a parallel task runner, which is not what the headline sells.

Checked against

The app does both: the Coordinator's create_workspaces and the screenplay-try-variants skill (3 versions in one Group by default) cover versions; the Create workspaces dialog covers separate tasks.

Proposed fix

Keep versions as the thesis, since it's the novel part and the headline already says it. Redraw Fig. 1 as one ask to the Coordinator ("Try three versions of the pricing hero") with its three Workspaces in one Group, side by side. Redraw Step 2 as the Coordinator proposing three Workspaces for that one ask. Parallel tasks become one sentence in the Coordinator feature card.

Recommendation

Do this first. It's the biggest lever on whether the page lands, and it only changes excerpts, not layout.

2
False claimHigh impact

"Works offline" and "your code stays on your machine" aren't true

Now

The Features card says the desktop app "works offline" and "your code stays on your machine". The FAQ says it "runs fully offline".

Checked against

Chat runs through Claude Code or Codex (AGENT_ENGINE=external in apps/desktop/desktop.env), which send code to their model provider. The chat adapter is fetched with npx -y on first use (lib/agent/harnesses/claude-code.ts:200). Repository detection sends the README and config files to the model (lib/add-repo/model-detect.ts). What is true: no account, no Screenplay servers, no telemetry, worktrees and a local database.

Proposed fix

Card: Runs on your Mac. No account and no Screenplay servers. Sandboxes are git worktrees on your disk and your canvases live in a local database. Your agent talks to its model provider, just as it does in your terminal.

FAQ, Does my code leave my machine? Only through your agent. The desktop app has no servers and no account; the CLI you already use sends code to its model provider, as it does today.

Recommendation

Fix now. It's a trust claim a developer can check in a minute, and being caught on it costs more than the claim earns.

3
False claimHigh impact

Knobs don't update every branch

Now

"Drag a slider and every branch updates without another prompt."

Checked against

Knob values are stored per frame (components/canvas/use-layer-mutations.ts:146): one slider changes one frame, synced to other viewers, never to other branches or back into code. Each branch has to call useKnob itself, which is why the popover offers "Ask the agent to add a knob" (knobs-popover.tsx:84).

Proposed fix

Knobs. Ask the agent to expose spacing, color or copy as knobs, then drag a slider to try values in a frame without another prompt.

Recommendation

Rewrite as above and drop the package name from the card; the docs link covers it.

4
False claimHigh impact

"Invite your team to review" is in the desktop flow

Now

How it works is the desktop flow (Step 1 is adding a repo to the app you just downloaded), and Step 3 ends "Invite your team to review."

Checked against

Sharing, cursors, following and comments are left out of the desktop build (components/canvas/canvas.tsx:2115, comments.tsx:782). Only the self-hosted web app has them.

Proposed fix

Step 3: Compare them live. Frames appear side by side as they build. Click through them and check phone sizes. (Teams stay in the Self-hosting section, which already says it well.)

Recommendation

Cut the sentence.

5
False claimHigh impact

The agent list is wrong for both ways of running it

Now

Features: "Run Claude Code, Codex or opencode with the accounts you already have." FAQ adds a built-in multi-provider agent. The page's meta description also lists opencode.

Checked against

opencode has no chat adapter (acpAdapter: null, lib/agent/harnesses/opencode.ts:266), so it only runs in terminal tabs. The built-in AI SDK agent is the hosted app's engine only (lib/agent/acp/engine-select.ts); on the hosted app, CLIs use the operator's shared keys, not your account. Choosing a model per chat is true.

Proposed fix

Card: Your agent, your account. Use Claude Code or Codex with the subscription you already have, and pick the model per chat.

FAQ: On the Mac, Claude Code or Codex through your own CLI and login; opencode runs in terminal tabs. Self-hosted, a built-in agent runs on the model keys your team configures (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, the Vercel AI Gateway or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint).

Recommendation

Fix with #2 in the same pass; both are about what runs where.

6
FrictionHigh impact

Download lands on a changelog, and only works on Apple Silicon

Now

Every Download button opens the GitHub Releases page. The latest release (0.1.4) opens with 60+ lines of internal PR titles (homepage dither, docs greys, favicon redirects) before the asset list. The button says "Download for Mac".

Checked against

The only build is Screenplay_<v>_aarch64.dmg (apps/desktop/scripts/release.mjs:213), so an Intel Mac user downloads an app that won't run. There's no auto-update (no updater plugin), so today's downloaders stay on today's build. The quickstart names Screenplay.dmg, which doesn't exist.

Proposed fix

Point the buttons straight at the file: have the release also upload a stable Screenplay.dmg and link releases/latest/download/Screenplay.dmg. Under the hero buttons, one small line: For Macs with Apple Silicon. Give releases a short user-facing summary above the generated PR list.

Recommendation

Do the direct link and the one-line requirement. (The cut "Apple Silicon · Runs fully local · MIT" line bundled three facts; this is one requirement at the moment it matters.) Auto-update is an app ticket, not a homepage one.

7
MissingMedium impact

"Before you download" never says what you need

Now

The FAQ is titled "Before you download." but has no requirements question. "Do I need to change my app?" says no, and that the npm packages give "synced state across frames".

Checked against

Real prerequisites: Apple Silicon, a Claude Code or Codex login (setup can install the CLI), git and Node (the chat adapter runs through npx), GitHub for pull requests (optional, lib/github-pr.ts:111). The dev server must listen on $PORT; Vite needs --port $PORT (docs, Dev server). Shared state is per frame, synced across viewers and play mode, not across frames.

Proposed fix

New first item, What do I need? A Mac with Apple Silicon, a Claude Code or Codex account (Screenplay can install the CLI), and a repository with a dev server. Connect GitHub if you want to open pull requests from the canvas.

Do I need to change my app? Usually not. Screenplay detects how to install and run it; the dev server just needs to use the port it's given. Two optional npm packages add knobs and shared state, and do nothing in production.

Recommendation

Add the item; it's the question the heading promises to answer.

8
OverstatedMedium impact

Self-hosting says "free" and lists half the stack

Now

"It's free and MIT licensed." The FAQ says it needs Vercel, Postgres and GitHub OAuth.

Checked against

It also needs Liveblocks, Vercel Blob, Vercel Sandbox VMs (billed per use) and at least one model API key, and everyone on the deployment shares the operator's keys (docs, Self-hosting overview table).

Proposed fix

Lede: Deploy the web app for your team and share a canvas. The software is free and MIT licensed; you pay for hosting and model usage.

FAQ: Deploy to Vercel with Postgres, Liveblocks, Vercel Blob and GitHub sign-in. Each Workspace runs in a Vercel Sandbox VM on your account, and the agent uses the model keys you set. Everyone on a canvas sees the same frames, cursors, comments and agent chats live.

Recommendation

Take it. A team lead who finds the extra bills later stops trusting the rest of the page.

9
StoryMedium impact

The problem blames agents for something you ask for

Now

"Agents write several versions. You see them one tab at a time."

Checked against

Agents don't write several versions by default; people ask for them. The first-run flow runs the first ask in one Workspace. The pain is real (the terminal on the left shows it well), but the subject of the sentence is wrong, so the reader has to agree with a premise before the pain.

Proposed fix

Headline: Three versions means three setups and three tabs. Body unchanged: Every worktree needs its own install, port and dev server, and each result lands in another browser tab.

Recommendation

Take it, or any wording that makes the reader the one who wants versions.

10
StaleMedium impact

Step 1 describes a "main Workspace" that doesn't exist

Now

"That becomes your main Workspace", and the excerpt shows a Workspace called Main installing dependencies.

Checked against

Adding a repository creates a fresh branch in its own worktree, titled New Workspace until the first ask names it (lib/fresh-workspace.ts, docs Quickstart). The product rule is that the UI never shows branch names, and "Main" reads as one.

Proposed fix

Add a repository. Screenplay works out how to run it and starts the dev server on a new branch. Your first Workspace appears on the canvas. (Excerpt row: New Workspace · Installing dependencies.)

Recommendation

Take it with the excerpt redraw in #1.

11
MissingMedium impact

Features picks weaker items and skips play mode

Now

Six cards: Live sandboxes, Coordinator, Pick elements, Knobs, agents, local. Step 4's menu already shows Open prototype player, but nothing says what it is.

Checked against

Unmentioned and shipped: play mode (full-window prototype with knobs, app/play/), record a flow (frames/Record), documents on the canvas the agent reads and writes, Plan mode, dev server logs the agent can read and restart. ⌘E only works while the chat composer has focus (components/agent/composer.tsx:662).

Proposed fix

Fold Pick elements into Live frames ("Pick any element from the chat with ⌘E to hand it to the agent.") and use the free card for Play mode: Open any frame full window and click through it like the real app, with its knobs beside it. Hand it to someone to try.

Recommendation

Take the swap. Documents and Plan mode are good docs material but don't sell the canvas.

12
CTALow impact

The hero's second button asks for a star

Now

Download for Mac, then Star on GitHub. The header already has a GitHub link.

Checked against

A team lead evaluating self-hosting has no way in from the hero; they have to scroll four sections. A star helps Screenplay, not the reader.

Proposed fix

Second button: Host it for your team, linking to #self-hosting. Keep GitHub in the header.

Recommendation

Optional. Worth it if teams are a real audience this month; skip it if the Mac app is the only goal for now.

13
StaleLow impact

The footer still sells the npm packages

Now

The Developers column lists @screenplay.space/knobs and @screenplay.space/state in mono.

Checked against

Zack cut the packages from the self-hosting pitch as an implementation detail (PR #1194). The footer is the last place they're sold.

Developers: Docs, GitHub, Self-hosting guide, Knobs guide (docs links).

Take it.

14
MissingLow impact

Shared links have no preview and an old description

Now

No Open Graph image (apps/homepage/app has only icon.ts). The meta description names opencode and says "ship the one that works".

Checked against

Links pasted into Slack, X or iMessage show a bare title. The description repeats the opencode error from #5.

Proposed fix

Add an opengraph-image rendering Fig. 1 under the headline. Description: Run your coding agents on separate branches and see every result live on one canvas. Free and open source, for Mac.

Recommendation

Take it; it's small and it's how most people will first see the page.

Checked on current main after PR #1194, with a production build of apps/homepage at 1280px. Claims were traced to code in apps/app and apps/desktop and to the docs. Out of scope here, and covered by the other homepage threads: layout, hierarchy, spacing and visual nits. What holds up: the headline, the terminal-versus-canvas contrast in The problem, the Coordinator claims, device sizes in frames, and opening a pull request from the canvas (once GitHub is connected).
